public_rationale: The conditional forecast cannot yet be scored because its antecedent is unverified. Tesla identifies formally independent directors and describes AI oversight responsibilities, but that does not establish the substantive independence implied by the passage or show that the predicted question was asked. No decisive event was found. With no deadline, missing public evidence is not a failed forecast.
limitations: A listing-rule reading of independence could change the condition status; the outcome would still remain unresolved without evidence of the board's discussion.
Private deliberations and inaccessible records limit the assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: An independent Tesla board will see Tesla's losses attributed to AI investment and a large supercomputer and ask when that spending will actually make the company money.

statement.excerpt: While Tesla has blamed some of its losses on "investing in AI" and "commissioning one of the world's largest supercomputers," these are the kind of things that an independent board will see and ask "when will it actually make us money?"

from_speaker: commissioning one of the world's largest supercomputers
when will it actually make us money?
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns board scrutiny of the financial returns from Tesla's AI and supercomputer spending. It does not predict a particular financial result.

In context, an independent board means a board able to exercise judgment independently of Musk. Classification of individual directors as independent under listing rules is relevant but does not conclusively establish this condition.
Asking when the investment will generate financial returns counts; the precise quoted wording is unnecessary.
criteria.support_condition: After the post, an independently functioning Tesla board questions when its AI and supercomputer spending will generate financial returns, documented by public statements, disclosed records, or credible reporting. The board-independence condition must also be established.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the independence condition is established, a sufficiently complete record conclusively shows that the qualifying board finished its oversight of the identified investments without questioning their financial returns. Silence in public disclosures or continued spending alone cannot establish this.

evidence.explanation: Tesla reports formal director independence, and the same filing describes board responsibility for overseeing AI strategy. These disclosures neither establish substantive independence from Musk for the relevant spending decisions nor record the predicted question.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence establishing an independently functioning Tesla board, together with dated records or credible reporting showing whether it questioned when the identified AI and supercomputer investments would generate financial returns.
